name: blume
short: Teaches your coding agent to build and maintain a docs site with Blume, a Markdown-first framework.
what: The core skill for Blume, an open-source docs framework on Astro and Vite. You drop Markdown or MDX into a folder and get a docs site with navigation, search, theming and Open Graph images. The skill teaches your agent to scaffold the site, write pages, edit `blume.config.ts` and run the Blume CLI. Blume also ships skills for migrating from other docs tools and keeping docs up to date.
who: Developers who want a docs site for a project and want their agent to do most of the setup and writing. If you're moving from Mintlify, Docusaurus or another docs tool, Blume's separate blume-migrate skill handles that.
needs: A coding agent that supports skills

steps.title: Install the skill
steps.text: Run it in the project where an agent will help with your docs.

steps.title: Scaffold a site
steps.text: This creates `docs/index.mdx` and `blume.config.ts`, adds dev and build scripts and installs dependencies.

steps.title: Build static HTML
steps.text: Output goes to `dist/`, with a local search index.

try.label: A first prompt
try.text: Use the blume skill to set up a docs site in this project and write a quickstart page.

watch: `npx blume migrate` and `blume upgrade --claude` or `--codex` hand work to Claude Code or Codex, which then edit your project.
The optional in-page assistant and MCP server need server output, set with a deploy adapter in `blume.config.ts`.
Blume generates a hidden `.blume/` folder on each run. Don't edit it. Run `npx blume eject` if you want a standalone Astro project.
